# SQLite

SQLite is a C-language library that implements a small, fast, self-contained, 
high-reliability, full-featured, SQL database engine. SQLite is the most used 
database engine in the world.

## What is SQLite?

SQLite is an embedded SQL database engine. Unlike most other SQL databases, 
SQLite does not have a separate server process. SQLite reads and writes 
directly to ordinary disk files. A complete SQL database with multiple tables, 
indices, triggers, and views, is contained in a single disk file.

## Where to Learn More

For comprehensive documentation about SQLite, including:
- How to use SQLite
- SQL syntax supported by SQLite
- Programming interfaces
- Performance characteristics
- Configuration options

Please visit the official SQLite website:

**[https://sqlite.org/](https://sqlite.org/)**

## Key Features

- **Serverless**: No separate server process required
- **Zero Configuration**: No setup or administration needed
- **Full-Featured**: Supports most of SQL92
- **Small Footprint**: Compact library, minimal memory usage
- **Reliable**: ACID transactions, even after system crashes
- **Cross-Platform**: Works on Unix, Windows, macOS, and many other systems

## License

SQLite is in the public domain. See [https://sqlite.org/copyright.html](https://sqlite.org/copyright.html) 
for details.

## Contact

- **Forum**: [https://sqlite.org/forum](https://sqlite.org/forum)
- **Website**: [https://sqlite.org/](https://sqlite.org/)

[https://sqlite.org/download.html](https://sqlite.org/download.html)
